test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a folk dance of Maharashtra?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Lavani.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lavani**

 
 
• **Lavani is a genre of music popular in Maharashtra.**
 
• It is a combination of traditional song and dance.
 
• It is particularly performed to the beats of **Dholki**, a percussion instrument.
 
• It has contributed substantially to the development of Marathi folk theatre.
 
• **In Maharashtra and southern Madhya Pradesh, it is performed by female performers wearing nine-yard-long sarees.**
 
• The songs are sung in a quick tempo.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baul**

 
 
• Baul dance connects love and spirituality.
 
• It aims to interact with the almighty in human beings’ souls.
 
• The modern Baul culture is very similar to western folk music.
 
• **It is a very prominent folk music tradition practiced in West Bengal.**
 
• The people have high regard for folk dance due to its highly spiritual and cosmic values.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**
 
 
• **The Bihu dance is an indigenous folk dance from the Indian state of Assam.**
 
• It is related to the **Bihu festival **and is an important part of Assamese culture.
 
• Bihu dancers are usually young men and women.
 
• The dancing style is characterized by brisk steps and rapid hand movements.
 
• The traditional costume of dancers is colorful and centered around the red color theme, signifying joy and vigor.
 
 
 
• **Mando**
 
 
• Mando is a musical form that evolved during the **19th and 20th centuries** among the Goan Catholics.
 
• It represents a meeting point of local Goan and western musical traditions.
 
• The dress worn during the Mando dance was of velvet or silk, red, blue, or green in color, embroidered with gold threads.
 
 
 
• The Mando festival at the Kala Academy, with performers, decked up for the event.
